name: Second Home Visa (E33)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a deposit of IDR 2 billion (approximately USD 130,000) in an Indonesian state-owned bank, placed within 90 days of visa approval or the visa lapses.
requirements.fix_path: Fund the qualifying deposit within 90 days of approval.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires Indonesian property valued at USD 1,000,000 or more, held under Hak Pakai (right-of-use) title, documented within 90 days of visa approval.
requirements.fix_path: Acquire and document qualifying property within 90 days of approval.

evidence_required.document: Bank deposit certificate or Hak Pakai property documentation

outcome.duration_length: 5 or 10 years (applicant's choice, likely tied to which financial tier is met), non-extendable beyond the chosen term

sources.title: Direktorat Jenderal Imigrasi eVisa portal -- Second Home Visa FAQ: 5-year (extendable) duration, no employment, family (including parents) can join, study permitted
Emerhub (immigration consultancy) -- Second Home Visa (E33): IDR 2 billion deposit or USD 1 million Hak Pakai property, 5 or 10 year options, parent-sponsorship allowed

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Indonesia's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT: an unreconciled discrepancy exists between the tier-1 eVisa FAQ (which describes a single 5-year, extendable duration) and the tier-3 source (which describes a fixed choice between 5-year and 10-year non-extendable terms) -- these were not resolved in this pass, so outcome.duration_length and renewable are stated per the tier-3 breakdown while flagging the tier-1 page's differing description explicitly rather than picking one silently. The specific deposit/property THRESHOLD figures are only tier-3 confirmed. Notably permissive family provision (confirmed at tier-1): parents of the principal may be sponsored, which most other Indonesian permit categories do not allow. TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT FINANCIAL GROUNDS modelled as OR-logic groups. dual_citizenship_allowed set false per Indonesia's general no-dual-citizenship rule (Law 12/2006) -- not specific to this visa.
